This Week in CPG (Jul 15, 2026); Fitt Insider Issue No. 409

fundNews.details: Coefficient Capital closed Fund II at $290M and its Apex growth vehicle at $240M, bringing total new capital under management to $500M. The firm focuses on consumer and retail technology investments. The dual-close structure signals strong LP appetite for consumer-focused venture strategies at both the early and growth stages.

Manica Blain, founder of Top Knot Ventures, joined Consumer VC podcast (Episode #362) to discuss the state of early-stage consumer VC. The conversation explored whether the asset class is broken and what it takes to build durable consumer brands in the current market environment.

Collaborative Fund raised $250M for Collab Holdings, a new private equity vehicle focused on consumer brands. The fund represents a significant shift from their venture roots into later-stage growth equity and PE buyouts. Strong LP demand for consumer-focused PE strategies underscores the maturation of the consumer brand investment ecosystem.

L Catterton and Patricof Co announced the formation of CHAMP, a strategic partnership connecting top athletes with consumer investment opportunities. The platform allows athletes including Kevin Durant, Cooper Flagg, Livvy Dunne, and Cade Cunningham to co-invest alongside L Catterton in emerging and scaled consumer brands. CHAMP represents a novel convergence of celebrity/athlete capital and institutional consumer VC deal access.

True Beauty Ventures kicked off fundraising for Fund III. Since launching in 2020, the firm has backed brands including Vacation, K18, Jupiter, Crown Affair, and Biologica. The fund focuses on beauty, wellness, and personal care investments.

S2G Investments secured $1B for Solutions Fund I, focused on backing growth-stage startups in Europe and North America across food, agriculture, and energy. Previous S2G investments include 80 Acres Farms, Apeel Sciences, Atomo Coffee, and Bettani Farms. The fund's scale signals strong LP appetite for sustainable food systems investing at the growth stage.

Mother Ventures closed a $10M fund to support companies building healthy futures for mothers and their families. The fund reflects growing institutional interest in the maternal health and family wellness category, building on strong consumer demand for products and services supporting the perinatal journey.

e.l.f. Beauty transferred ownership of Keys Soulcare back to co-founder Alicia Keys as of May 21, 2026. The brand exit was announced during e.l.f.'s earnings call as the company refocuses on its five core growth brands including e.l.f. Cosmetics, rhode, Naturium, and W3LL People. Keys Soulcare was originally co-founded and incubated by e.l.f. in 2020.

fundNews.details: Shein acquired San Francisco-based apparel brand Everlane for approximately $100 million. Everlane, known for its radical transparency positioning and minimalist staples, had been struggling with $90 million in debt. The brand will retain operational autonomy and its sustainability commitments under Shein ownership.

fundNews.fund: Heartland Food Products Group / Whole Earth Brands
fundNews.details: Heartland Food Products Group, the owner of Splenda, acquired the Americas business of Whole Earth Brands and its broad portfolio of natural sweeteners. Heartland now owns a diversified sweetener portfolio including Equal, Swerve, Whole Earth, Chuker, and Splenda. The deal consolidates two major players in the better-for-you sweetener category.

Scholl's Wellness Company, parent of the Dr. Scholl's brand, acquired performance-focused insole maker VKTRY. VKTRY is known for its carbon fiber insoles used by elite athletes to enhance performance and reduce injury risk. The acquisition expands Dr. Scholl's portfolio into the performance footwear innovation segment.

UK-based Imperial Brands (through ITG Brands) acquired tobacco alternative brand Black Buffalo for $150M plus earnout. Black Buffalo was founded in 2015 and backed by Listen Ventures, Vice Ventures, Access Capital, and Watchfire Ventures. The exit represents a notable consumer CPG M&A outcome for early-stage backers in the smokeless tobacco alternatives space.

Global dairy giant Lactalis acquired UK-based sports nutrition brand Protein Works for an undisclosed sum. Protein Works, founded in 2012 in Liverpool, generates ~$75M in annual sales across protein supplements and nutrition products. The deal follows Danone's $1.15B acquisition of Huel earlier in 2026, signaling accelerating Big Food/Dairy consolidation into functional nutrition.

fundNews.fund: Church & Dwight / Miss Mouth's Messy Eater
fundNews.details: Church & Dwight (NYSE: CHD) acquired Miss Mouth's Messy Eater for $325M. Thrasio had purchased the brand in 2020 and scaled it into the largest stain remover brand on Amazon, generating $80M net sales and $28M EBITDA in 2025. The acquisition continues Church & Dwight's disciplined acquisition playbook and highlights how Amazon-native brands can achieve significant strategic exits.

Animal Capital closed Fund III with $33 million in total commitments on June 10, 2026. Led by founder Marshall Sandman, the fund nearly doubles the firm's prior vehicle and targets early-stage, primarily U.S.-based consumer tech investments that leverage technology to improve consumer lives. Fund III increases the firm's target check size by approximately 150% versus its inaugural fund.

Anti Fund, the growth-stage investment firm co-founded by Jake Paul and Geoffrey Woo, raised $100M for its debut growth fund. While largely focused on tech, Anti Fund has also backed consumer brands including OLIPOP, Happy Dad, Ketone-IQ, Khloud, SipMargs, and Sesh. The raise signals growing crossover between celebrity/athlete-backed capital and institutional growth investing.

Consumer-focused investment firm InvestEco raised $106M CAD for Fund IV. Since launching in 2002, InvestEco has backed LesserEvil Snacks, Little Sesame, Mid-Day Squares, Algae Cooking Club, Om Mushroom Superfood, and other consumer startups. The firm expects to make another 6 to 10 investments from Fund IV over the next few years.

Avenir Collective, a former Amazon aggregator known as Olsam Group, acquired Australian skincare and wrinkle patch brand Wrinkles Schminkles. Founded by Gabrielle Requena and based in Sydney, the bootstrapped brand does around $14M in annual sales.

Private equity firm ACON Investments acquired YumEarth, an early mover in the better-for-you candy category founded in 2007. The Stamford, CT-based brand is best known for organic, allergy-friendly candy and retails at 30,000 stores including Target, Walmart, Kroger, and Sprouts.
AI-enabled telehealth provider OpenLoop Health acquired Hey Revia, a platform that uses AI to automate complex healthcare phone calls, expanding OpenLoop's operational automation capabilities.
Private equity firm CVC Capital Partners acquired Spanish gym chain Enjoy! Wellness, extending CVC's footprint in the European fitness and wellness sector.

Premium spirits company Edrington, owner of Macallan, officially sold its majority (80%) stake in Wyoming Whiskey to WW Partners, led by Wyoming Whiskey co-founder David DeFazio. Edrington first acquired a minority stake in 2018 before upping it to 80% in 2023.

New Orleans-based spirits giant Sazerac acquired Garrard County Distilling for $20M at a court-ordered auction. Garrard operates a 50,000-square-foot distillery south of Lexington, Kentucky, and the deal continues Sazerac's acquisition spree.

Hormel Foods exited Brazil, selling its local operations to Zanchetta Alimentos LTDA as part of its ongoing portfolio streamlining. The move follows Hormel's sale of a 51% stake in Justin's last year.

Citation Capital closed its inaugural fund with $1.2B in total commitments. Founded in 2023 by Tiffany Hagge and Lydie Hudson, the firm specializes in mid-cap buyouts across services, industrial, and consumer sectors, and previously acquired a majority stake in snack manufacturer Cibo Vita.

Hockey Stick Ventures launched its $3M Fund I. Founded by Sean Hershman in late 2023, the firm has already backed Recess, The Coconut Cult, Renais Gin, Leisure Hydration, Slate Milk, De Soi, and Liquid Death.

points.label: a16z Leads Telepatia's $33M Series A — Conversational AI Consumer Apps Hit Institutional Scale
points.context: Andreessen Horowitz led Telepatia's $33M Series A this week, backing an AI-native consumer application in the conversational/companion AI category. The round signals that a16z — after years of writing checks in AI infrastructure — is now deploying at Series A in consumer-facing AI applications with confidence. Telepatia represents the category's maturation from 'interesting experiment' to 'institutionally fundable at scale' within a single product cycle.
points.take: Founders building AI-native consumer apps should treat a16z's Telepatia conviction as a category legitimization signal — Series A conversations with institutional funds are now viable for conversational AI consumer products that can demonstrate retention and monetization, even without the scale benchmarks that pre-AI consumer apps required to cross the seed-to-A threshold.

points.label: Consumer Hardware Sees Four Deals in One Week — The Category Is No Longer Being Skipped
points.context: Four consumer hardware deals closed this week across different price points and use cases: Temple ($54M Growth, sleep tech), Solius Labs ($23M Series A, light therapy backed by Lauder Partners), Claire ($11.6M Seed, Khosla Ventures), and Kimba ($6.5M Seed, Selva Ventures). The breadth of stages — from seed to growth — and the caliber of lead investors (Khosla, Lauder Partners) signals that hardware-native consumer companies are no longer systematically avoided by top-tier VCs.
points.take: Consumer hardware founders at the seed and Series A stage now have four recent comps with named institutional leads to anchor valuation conversations — the Solius Labs Series A (Lauder Partners) and Claire Seed (Khosla Ventures) are particularly useful because both were hardware-first bets by funds not historically associated with hardware risk, signaling an expansion of the lead investor pool beyond specialist hardware funds.

points.label: Everlab's A$65M (~$46M) Series A in Australia Illustrates Global Consumer Health Tech's Institutional Moment
points.context: Australian longevity and preventive health platform Everlab raised A$65M (~$46M) in a Series A led by Airtree Ventures — the largest consumer health Series A to close outside the US/UK this week. Alongside French health tech rocapin's $13M Series A (Educapital), the week saw two non-US consumer health platforms reaching institutional scale. Both companies leverage personalized health data to drive preventive consumer health decisions.
points.take: Global consumer health tech at the Series A stage is no longer a US-centric opportunity — Everlab and rocapin together signal that leading non-US VCs (Airtree in ANZ, Educapital in Europe) are deploying conviction capital into consumer health platforms, meaning US-based founders in the category now face international competition for the same category leadership positions and should accelerate international go-to-market strategies before these platforms establish global network effects.

points.label: Longevity-Adjacent Consumer Plays Are Clustering: Solius, Gero, Rejoni All Raise in the Same Week
points.context: Three companies targeting biological aging or longevity mechanisms closed rounds this week: Solius Labs ($23M Series A, photobiomodulation light therapy), Gero ($17M Growth, AI-driven longevity biomarker platform), and Rejoni ($25M Growth, cellular regeneration). All three attack different points on the longevity stack — hardware delivery, biomarker diagnostics, and cellular biology — suggesting the category is broad enough to support parallel institutional bets rather than being winner-take-all.
points.take: The simultaneous institutional backing of three longevity-adjacent companies at different scientific and commercial stages validates a portfolio theory for the category — founders and VCs considering longevity bets should scope which of the three longevity layers (hardware delivery, diagnostics, intervention) they are positioned in and use Solius/Gero/Rejoni as the reference comps for each layer rather than treating 'longevity' as a monolithic category with a single market leader.

points.label: Rhoback's $50M CHAMP-Led Round: Athlete Capital Is Now Writing Growth Equity Checks
points.context: Performance apparel brand Rhoback raised $50M in a growth equity round led by CHAMP — the recently formed platform partnership between L Catterton and Patricof Co that enables elite athletes including Kevin Durant, Cooper Flagg, and Livvy Dunne to co-invest in consumer brands. L Catterton and Patricof Co also participated directly. The round illustrates how CHAMP is being deployed as a lead investment vehicle rather than purely an athlete endorsement overlay.
points.take: CHAMP's emergence as a lead investor in growth-stage consumer brands — rather than a celebrity co-investment sidecar — changes the composition of competitive growth equity rounds for premium apparel and active lifestyle brands. Founders in the $30-75M growth range should now evaluate CHAMP as a strategic lead candidate whose athlete network provides a distribution advantage that pure financial VCs cannot replicate, particularly for performance and lifestyle brands where athlete authenticity drives conversion.

points.label: L'Oreal Acquires Innovist: Big Beauty's India Strategy Is Acquisition-Led
points.context: L'Oreal acquired Indian skincare brand Innovist this week, following a pattern of global beauty conglomerates building India exposure through acquisition rather than organic market entry. Innovist joins a growing list of Indian direct-to-consumer beauty brands that have exited to strategic acquirers as India's skincare and personal care market matures. The deal reflects Big Beauty's accelerating recognition that India is a must-win market requiring local brand equity rather than export-driven growth.
points.take: The L'Oreal/Innovist acquisition opens a clearer exit thesis for India-born consumer beauty brands at the seed and Series A stage — founders building in the Indian personal care category should now be pitching to global beauty strategics not just as future distribution partners but as potential acquirers in the 3-5 year horizon, using the Innovist exit as a proof point that India-native brand equity is valued at the M&A level by top-tier global strategics.

points.label: Anti Fund's $100M Debut: Celebrity-Backed Growth Vehicles Are Institutionalizing at Scale
points.context: Anti Fund, co-founded by Jake Paul and Geoffrey Woo, closed a $100M debut growth fund targeting consumer brands including prior bets on OLIPOP, Happy Dad, Ketone-IQ, Khloud, and SipMargs. The raise follows CHAMP's formation and reflects a broader institutionalization of celebrity and athlete-backed investment vehicles — where the LP relationship and co-investment access are themselves the structural value add, rather than just brand endorsement. Anti Fund's $100M scale places it firmly in the institutional growth equity tier.
points.take: The $100M Anti Fund close signals that consumer founders seeking growth capital should evaluate celebrity-backed institutional vehicles (Anti Fund, CHAMP) as legitimate lead candidates rather than soft capital sources — the combination of institutional check size, portfolio network effects across co-invested brands, and authentic consumer reach is a differentiated value proposition that traditional growth equity funds cannot easily replicate for brands targeting younger or wellness-adjacent consumer demographics.
